proposed.explanation: This is arid-climate doctrine; it fails in tropics where nighttime temps are too high. Tropical orientation prioritizes shade and ventilation, not winter heating gain (unnecessary in tropics). Reflectance helps but is secondary to active air movement strategies. The hierarchy: 'In tropical climates, ventilation is the primary cooling mechanism—not shade alone, not mass, not orientation.' Nighttime temps (22–25°C) prevent thermal mass from radiating stored daytime heat.
